text:
Changing the control-divider ratio should fix both failures, so I'll steer the numerical refiner rather than rewrite the program.

The ring oscillates at mid and high control voltage (3.07 GHz and 4.89 GHz), but at Vctrl = 0.7 V it gives no frequency and only 0.5 mV swing. With div = 0.85, the starving gate sits at about 0.595 V, which is deep subthreshold. That makes the predicted f_lo about 27 MHz, which is likely too slow to start up within the simulation window. Both failures come from that one cause.

Raising div to about 0.91 should increase the starving current at the low end roughly 3–5×. That would put f_lo near 120–170 MHz, so the ring starts and swings rail-to-rail. It would still keep fmax/fmin above 29, because fmax is already close to the inverter-limited ceiling. Power at mid scales up modestly from 0.32 mW and should stay well under 1.1 mW.

```json
{"action": "refine",
 "reason": "Ring stalls at vctrl=0.7 V (vg≈0.595 V, deep subthreshold, ~30 MHz) so swing/f_lo fail. Raise divider ratio to lift low-end current 3-5x (f_lo ~150 MHz) keeping ratio >29; f_mid, power have margin.",
 "params": {"div": 0.91, "mrat": 5.0, "ws": 6.0},
 "bounds": {"div": [0.87, 0.97], "ws": [3.0, 12.0]}}
```
